# ListView

**Class:** `UltraCanvasListView` · **Group:** [Navigation and data views](../Groups/Navigation-and-data-views.md) · **Header:** [`UltraCanvas/include/UltraCanvasListView.h`](../../../UltraCanvas/include/UltraCanvasListView.h) · `#include "UltraCanvasListView.h"`

**Inherits:** [`UltraCanvasUIElement`](UltraCanvasUIElement.md) → `Element`

## What it is for

List **or table** — `UltraCanvasListView` is the multi-column, virtualised, model-driven one (`IListModel` + `ListColumnDef` + delegates; `SetShowHeader(true)` gives resizable columns, header tooltips and a sort indicator; sort and filter it with [`UltraCanvasListSortFilterProxy`](../../UltraCanvas/UltraCanvasListSortFilterProxy.md)); tree; multi-column tree ([`UltraCanvasColumnsTreeView`](../../UltraCanvas/UltraCanvasTreeViewExamples.md#columnar-layout-ultracanvascolumnstreeview): aligned Name / Type / Value columns with a header band, resizable boundaries and section-header rows); sheet

## Creating it

Constructors:

```cpp
UltraCanvasListView(const std::string& identifier, float x, float y, float w, float h);
UltraCanvasListView(const std::string& identifier, float w, float h);
explicit UltraCanvasListView(const std::string& identifier);
```

The first string argument is always the element's **identifier**, never its text (see [Core concepts](../Core-Concepts.md#identifiers)).

## Callbacks

Assign a lambda to the member (or call the setter). Capture the element and its parents **raw**, never as a `shared_ptr` - see [Events and callbacks](../Events-and-Callbacks.md#ownership).

| Callback | Signature | When it fires |
|---|---|---|
| `onItemClicked` | `std::function<void(int row)> onItemClicked` | _Item clicked_ |
| `onItemDoubleClicked` | `std::function<void(int row)> onItemDoubleClicked` | _Item double clicked_ |
| `onItemActivated` | `std::function<void(int row)> onItemActivated` | _Item activated_ |
| `onSelectionChanged` | `std::function<void(const std::vector<int>&)> onSelectionChanged` | _Selection changed_ |
| `onItemHovered` | `std::function<void(int row)> onItemHovered` | _Item hovered_ |
| `onKeyDown` | `std::function<bool(const UCEvent&)> onKeyDown` | A key pressed in the view reaches this before the view's own handling (the arrows, Return): true consumes it. A dropdown's open list takes typed letters this way, to go to the item starting with them. |
| `onCellClicked` | `std::function<void(int row, int column, const Point2Di& posInCell)> onCellClicked` | Cell-level callbacks (multi-column aware). posInCell is relative to the cell's top-left corner, i.e. the same space as the rects a delegate computes from ListItemStyleOption (x - columnX, y - row top). Hover is reported on every mouse move; (row=-1, column=-1) means the pointer left the rows area. |
| `onCellHovered` | `std::function<void(int row, int column, const Point2Di& posInCell)> onCellHovered` | _Cell hovered_ |
| `onCellDoubleClicked` | `std::function<void(int row, int column, const Point2Di& posInCell)> onCellDoubleClicked` | A double-click on a cell, after onItemDoubleClicked: which column it hit, for an owner that edits the cell in place. |
| `onHeaderClicked` | `std::function<void(int column)> onHeaderClicked` | A click (press and release in the same cell) on a column header, when the header is shown. Fires after a press that did not start a column resize. The usual handler re-sorts the model by `column`, toggling the direction when it is already the sort column, then calls SetSortIndicator so the header shows the new order. |
| `onContextMenu` | `std::function<void(int row, const UCEvent& event)> onContextMenu` | A right-button press in the rows area. `row` is the row under the pointer, -1 for the empty space below the rows; a row under the pointer is selected first (alone), as every desktop does, so the handler's menu acts on what the user pointed at (unless SetSelectsOnContextMenu(false) says otherwise). The usual handler … |
| `tooltipProvider` | `std::function<std::string(int row, int column)> tooltipProvider` | Optional tooltip source, consulted before the model's ToolTipRole. Called with the hovered cell; row == -1 means the pointer is over the header cell of `column`. Returning an empty string falls back to the model tooltip (ToolTipRole) or, for the header, to ListColumnDef::tooltip. |

- from [`UltraCanvasUIElement`](UltraCanvasUIElement.md): `eventCallback`, `onPopupAboutToClose`, `onPopupClosed`, `onPopupOpened`, `SetEventCallback`

| `OnModelChanged` | `virtual void OnModelChanged()` | After the view has taken in a change its model signalled - the rows replaced, one changed, inserted or removed. A subclass that keeps something derived from the rows (a column fitted to their text) marks it stale here, rather than wrapping the model's callbacks, which would outlive it. |

### struct `ScrollMetrics`

What the scrollbars are computed from, as of now: the rows and their total height, the columns and their total width, the viewport the rows get (less whichever scrollbar shows), the resulting ranges, and where each scrollbar sits (element-local) and whether it shows. For diagnostics and tests; every value is what UpdateScrollbar would use if it ran at this moment.

| Field | Declaration | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `rows` | `int rows = 0` |  |
| `rowHeight` | `int rowHeight = 0` | uniform rows; 0 when the delegate sizes them |

| `viewportHeight` | `int viewportHeight = 0` | the rows area: header and horizontal scrollbar excluded |

| `scrollOffset` | `int scrollOffset = 0` |  |

| `viewportWidth` | `int viewportWidth = 0` |  |
| `maxScrollX` | `int maxScrollX = 0` | contentWidth - viewportWidth, floored at 0 |
| `scrollOffsetX` | `int scrollOffsetX = 0` |  |

### struct `ColumnFitting`

Every column fitted to its content (multi-column), with those two measurements, at the next paint after the model's rows or columns change - the one moment a render context is at hand: each column becomes as wide as its widest DisplayRole text in `font` plus `padding` (what the delegate leaves beside the text; the default delegate's is 6 px each side), never narrower than its header's title and sort triangle, and within [minWidth, maxWidth] (maxWidth 0: no cap) - so one long text does not take the whole grid. The fit stops once the user drags a border (ColumnsUserAdjusted), and a SetColumnWidth of the caller's holds until the next fit. Off by default: the model's ListColumnDef::width is the width.

| Field | Declaration | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `bool enabled = false` |  |
| `font` | `FontStyle font` |  |
| `padding` | `int padding = 12` |  |
| `minWidth` | `int minWidth = 40` |  |
| `maxWidth` | `int maxWidth = 0` |  |
